<!-- pr-reviewer: c4cab3dcea15e115026ff717f29c2f9fcacbbcb8 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after the maintainer's hand check of the new Fixtures-page controls - see Notes).

Reviewed at the high tier (fixtures feed the collision checks).

**What looks good**
- Both edits are undoable commands (`SetModJaw`, `RefitModVise`, `crates/app/src/commands/mod_vise_edit.rs`), one history step each. `invert` restores the previous mesh (via `UpdateModel`), the previous `FixtureDef` marker and the previous pose, in the same step. All validation happens at command creation (`SetModJaw::new` :71, `RefitModVise::new` :140), so a refusal moves nothing.
- Both have MCP tools (`set_mod_jaw`, `refit_mod_vise` in `mcp/modvise_tools.rs`) that call the same commands; the UI queues the same commands through `CommandKind`.
- No stale-clear risk found: the workholding/clash verdicts are derived from the fixture's current def, mesh and pose and are not cached; the edit's own check runs at creation against the new shape and pose (`face_gap` before/after via the shared `judge_face`, plate seat, `footprint_at`, `after_fixture_shape` clash warnings). A face that reaches into the stock is refused; a lift-off or a shape landing in a part/stock is a returned warning, shown in the status line / MCP `warning`.
- The #833 probe (jaw from beside the stock to 16 mm inside it) is now refused through `judge_face` (`commands/mod_vise.rs`), pinned by `a_plate_edit_that_brings_a_jaw_into_a_stock_it_was_beside_is_refused`.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in the new non-test code; `quarter()` refuses non-quarter turns by name. No new keys, so save/load is unchanged (round-trip test included). Decision record present, no snapshot PNG or CHANGELOG edits, no build.rs/.github/scripts/dependency changes, no process files touched. Held-back dual-station block is explained and `Refs #832` keeps the issue open.

**Local results** (trial-merged with `upstream/main`, clean merge, no conflicts)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app` tests: mod_vise_edit (6), mod_vise (5), mod_vise_plate (6), mcp_mod_vise (2), mcp_plate (1), fixture_plate (7), fixture_plate_riders (7), fixture_keys_lenient (3), fixtures (14) | all pass |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (crates/ui) | 5 `law_tests` (gizmo/height_plane) failed in parallel, a known flake; re-run `--test-threads=1`: 534 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-ui --test fixtures` | 7 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I ran the suites the diff touches, not the whole quick plan (the author reports the full quick gate green on this head).

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. UI part: the "Edit jaw block..." draft and "Re-fit to stock" controls are covered by structural tests only. A clean verdict still needs the maintainer's hand check of those controls in the real app.
2. Editing the fixed block's figures (e.g. `face_offset`) does not re-judge the adjustable partner, which stays where it was; the pair may then no longer touch the stock until "Re-fit to stock" is used. The status/doc hint to re-fit is there only for the edited block's own face. Consider a follow-up warning.
3. `crates/ui/src/state.rs` is already ~4.3k lines (grew by 13); a split is worth a follow-up, not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
